name: App Builder & Ownership — approval frames
description: Contract-freeze UX artifacts for docs/planning/app-builder-and-ownership.md (rollout item F-2). Four flows: (1) a 'Build your application' card beside the dashed 'Add application' card on /applications; (2) the build session — form (where/name/brief), progress (launching → building → deploying → deployed), FuzeAgent deep link, cancel, and every terminal/refusal state; (3) the org-held, user-originated ownership block in app detail (org as owner, creator name+contact while a member, 'former member' after); (4) the marketplace publish request and the platform-admin review queue. Each flow ships dark behind its own default-OFF release flag. Approving a flow approves its visual + interaction model AND its component/package/contract build inventory. Flows bind to the REAL @fuzefront/app-registry-client (app-registry 1.2.0, #1261); two additive contract amendments are commissioned by approval (see commissionedByApproval).

coordination.frontend/src/pages/ApplicationsPage.tsx: Also claimed by design/frames/app-management (feature-level implementation.paths; flows unapproved). build-entry claims it too, so gate-frames-first passes the card mount once build-entry is approved (one approved claiming flow suffices). The page change is limited to importing and mounting <BuildAppCard /> after the Add-application card; the card's markup/logic live in packages/app-builder-ui/src/entry/**. Any other change to ApplicationsPage remains app-management's to approve.
coordination.app detail (/apps/:appId): Owned by app-management/app-detail (AppDetailFlow, packages/app-management-ui). Flows creator-ownership and marketplace-publish ship self-contained components (AppOwnershipCard, PublicationPanel) from packages/app-builder-ui that AppDetailFlow mounts; they claim only their own package paths, so they never block or are blocked by app-detail's approval.
coordination.routes (/applications/build[/:sessionId]: Registered in frontend/src/App.tsx as one-line mounts of BuildSessionFlow and PublicationReviewQueue from @fuzefront/app-builder-ui. App.tsx is shell plumbing (governance/frames-first-policy.json nonFeaturePaths), so it is deliberately not claimed here; all feature UI lives under packages/app-builder-ui/**.

commissionedByApproval: AppCreator.contactEmail (string, optional) — returned under the same rule as displayName: only while isCurrentMember is true. app-registry 1.2.0 has no contact channel on AppCreator; frame (e1)'s Contact row needs it. Until contract-designer lands it (1.3.0, additive/minor) the UI renders the creator's name and omits the Contact row — never a guessed address.

GET /publication-requests?status=pending (platform admin only, cursor-paginated, flag fuzefront.apps.marketplace-publishing) returning AppPublication plus app displayName/icon/organizationId — app-registry 1.2.0 can approve/reject per app but cannot list what is pending. Flow 4's review queue (frame g) cannot be implemented until it lands; the frames deliberately do not invent a client-side scan of GET /apps.
Polling cadence for in-flight build sessions (no push channel in the contract): 5 s for the first minute, backing off to 30 s, paused while hidden, stopped at a terminal status (frame c).

designSystemAdditions: Stepper — ordered progress with done/current/failed/cancelled step states (build progress)
RadioCardGroup — keyboard-navigable choice cards, role=radiogroup (build target)
TextareaWithCounter — length-limited textarea with live counter and over-limit state (brief ≤4000, notes/reason ≤2000)
StatusPill, Dialog, DataTable — already requested by app-management (dsPrimitivesNeeded); reuse, do not duplicate

frames.label: (a) Build your application card
frames.summary: The Applications grid with the new solid, seam-topped 'Build your application' card immediately after the dashed 'Add application' card. Flag OFF, flag-resolving and in-flight-session (resume shortcut) variants.
frames.acceptanceNotes: With fuzefront.apps.build-with-agent ON the grid renders [data-card='build-application'] directly after [data-action='add-application']; it is role=button, tabIndex 0, activated by click/Enter/Space, and routes to /applications/build. With the flag OFF the element is NOT in the DOM (not disabled, not CSS-hidden), and no /build-sessions request is made. While the flag is resolving it is treated as OFF — no flash-in. When GET /build-sessions?limit=1 returns a non-terminal session, the card becomes [data-action='resume-build-session'] linking to /applications/build/:sessionId.

frames.label: (b) Describe the app
frames.summary: The build form: where (personal workspace / active org as radio cards, defaulting to current context), name (1–120), brief (1–4000 with live counter). Personal-only, validation and submitting states.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Target defaults to the current context; the organization option is rendered only when the caller has an active membership in the active org. Submit sends POST /build-sessions with CreateBuildSessionRequest {context, organizationId?, name, brief}: organizationId present iff context=organization; never an id. Name empty or brief >4000 disables [data-action='start-build'] and shows inline errors; a 400 VALIDATION from the server renders the same way, inline. While submitting, inputs lock and exactly one request is in flight. 201 navigates to /applications/build/:id. Any refusal keeps the form values (frame d).

frames.label: (c) Session in progress
frames.summary: Reload-safe session page: 4-step stepper (launching/building/deploying/deployed; requested folds into launching), status pill, FuzeAgent deep link, session meta and brief, cancel with confirm dialog, loading skeleton.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Renders from GET /build-sessions/{id}; polls while status is requested/launching/building/deploying (5 s for the first minute, then 30 s; paused when hidden; stops at terminal). Exactly one step has data-step-state='current'. [data-action='open-agent-session'] renders only when agentSessionUrl is non-null AND resolves to the shell's own origin; otherwise [data-state='agent-link-pending'] (null) or nothing (cross-origin) — never a dead or off-site link. [data-action='cancel-build'] shows for requester/org managers while in-flight and opens a confirm; [data-action='confirm-cancel-build'] calls POST /build-sessions/{id}/cancel. A 409 on cancel means the session went terminal first: refetch and render it, no error toast.

frames.label: (d) Outcomes, failures & refusals
frames.summary: Terminal states (deployed with the new app tile on Applications, failed with errorCode/errorMessage, cancelled) and every refusal: 502 launch_failed, 503 builder_unavailable, 503 feature_disabled, 403 not a member, 409 no_personal_org, 429, 404 session not found, and a transient polling error.
frames.acceptanceNotes: deployed: success banner with [data-action='open-app'] for appSlug; the Applications list query is invalidated so the app tile appears via the normal GET /apps (no special-casing). failed: show errorMessage (as text) and errorCode, offer [data-action='start-new-build']; no app added. cancelled: terminal notice + start-new-build. 502 → launch_failed with retry, form kept. 503 builder_unavailable → nothing created, offer Add application. 503 feature_disabled → not-available page. 403 → in place (never a sign-in redirect), offer building in the personal workspace. 409 no_personal_org → choose an org. 429 → wait, form kept. 404 (unknown or not entitled) → 'not found', never distinguishing forbidden. A failed poll keeps the last known state ([data-state='stale']) and retries — it is not a failed build.

frames.label: (e) Owner & creator
frames.summary: Ownership block in app detail: the owning org first; creator name + contact while a current member; 'Former member' with no name or contact after they leave; personal app (you are owner and creator); creator not recorded; flag OFF (block absent); loading.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Owner always renders from App.organizationId (personal org → 'Your personal workspace'). creator.isCurrentMember=true → displayName ([data-field='creator-name']) and, once AppCreator.contactEmail exists, [data-action='contact-creator']; until then the Contact row is omitted. creator.isCurrentMember=false → [data-field='creator-former'] 'Former member' and the UI renders NO name or contact even if present in the payload. creator=null → 'Not recorded'. If the response lacks the creator key (fuzefront.apps.creator-ownership OFF) the block is not rendered at all. The block shows no roles and no authority controls.

frames.label: (f) Publish to marketplace
frames.summary: Publishing panel in app detail: tier badge + review state. none → 'Publish to marketplace' + request dialog with optional notes; pending; approved (marketplace tier); rejected with reason + resubmit; 409 ALREADY_PENDING / ALREADY_PUBLISHED; read-only (panel absent); 403 on submit.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Panel renders only when fuzefront.apps.marketplace-publishing is ON and GET /apps/{slug}/publication returns 200 (a 404 means the caller can't manage the app → no panel, no control). status none or rejected shows [data-action='request-publication']; submit is POST /apps/{slug}/publication-requests {target:'marketplace', notes?} (notes ≤2000). pending shows no request control. approved shows tier marketplace. rejected shows rejection.reason verbatim as text. A 409 (ALREADY_PENDING / ALREADY_PUBLISHED) is a race: refetch and render the current state. A 403 on submit is shown in place and the control is removed.

frames.label: (g) Admin review queue
frames.summary: Platform-admin queue of pending requests (app, publisher org, creator contact per the frame-e rule, notes, submitted), approve dialog with optional note, reject dialog with required reason, 409 NOT_PENDING race, empty, loading, error, 403.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Rows come from the ANTICIPATED GET /publication-requests?status=pending (commissioned; not in 1.2.0), oldest first, cursor-paginated. [data-action='confirm-approve-publication'] calls POST /apps/{slug}/publication-requests/approve {notes?}. [data-action='confirm-reject-publication'] is disabled until a 1–2000 char reason is entered, then calls …/reject {reason}. Both remove the row optimistically and restore it on non-2xx, except 409 NOT_PENDING which removes it with a notice. A former-member creator is never named. Non-platform-admins get 403 in place and no nav entry.
